note: How the people of the open world's towns talk to the heir (core/game/game_talk.gd; the words are in data/text/talk.json, the `talk` catalog, so they can be translated; checked by tools/check_data.gd). Everything is a pure function of the seed, the person's id, the day, the hour and the heir's tile: no dice of the dynasty's, nothing saved. USE beside a person (within `reach_street` tiles of one out of doors, within `reach_house` of one inside a building whose roof is lifting) and they say something: their job's line for the time (day or night), then `extras` more things picked from what fits (the weather, the family's standing with the town's faction, whether the family has built a house, their own or the heir's size, their race, their town), all by an id hash that changes every `hour_block` hours; a sleeper only mumbles. A person may also talk first: when the heir comes within `call_range` tiles of one (`call_range_house` for one inside a building) who is awake and has not spoken today, a hash of the seed, their id, the day and the heir's tile decides (`chance_percent`, `gate_percent` for a gate guard); at most one greeting a day for each person, and `cooldown_seconds` of the world clock between any two; the screen never asks during a fight or while a panel is open. A person of a job in `conversations` also offers a few `choices` (`news` a rumour of a creature seen near the town, `fear` the same as a warning, `wares` what their service offers); a rumour is the creature GameSpawn would put on a tile `rumour.min` to `rumour.max` tiles from the town's anchor, found by up to `rumour.tries` hashes of the seed, the town and the day. `bubble_seconds` is how long a line stays over a head.
